subject: Agriculture
title: Roman Farming and Latifundia
description: One-minute skill: Roman Farming and Latifundia.

hook.text: Rome started as a farming republic. Small farmers served as soldiers. Then plantations swallowed them.

buildup.text: Wealthy Romans built latifundia—huge estates worked by enslaved people, growing olives, grapes, and grain.

discovery.text: Latifundia produced cheaply at scale, underselling small farmers who couldn't compete.

twist.text: Displaced farmers flooded into Rome, creating an urban poor class. The social fabric of the republic tore.

climax.text: Some historians argue that the shift from small farms to plantations helped bring down the Roman Republic.

punchline.text: Rome's farms grew larger. Its republic grew weaker.

quiz.question: What were latifundia in the Roman Empire?
options: Large agricultural estates worked by enslaved labor
